docs.title: LLM Providers Table
docs.text:
What is this for?

Here you will find free, freemium, and paid providers, that provide access to large language models. It includes limits, registration requirements, the ability to quickly copy the Base URL, and direct links for registration/getting an API key.

Help tablet! Share it!

The more people who use it, the more motivated I'll be to update it, add new providers, and keep everything up to date. Post a link to the table in chat, in repo, in comments, or on Discord server - anywhere 🙏

Relevance

Providers change limits, models, and sometimes even die... I am just one person, but there are many providers, so I don't always have time to update table. If there are any discrepancies with the real situation at the provider, please inform me! Via on Telegram or DS - Ner_Kun.

For roleplayers

Friends, if you, like me, roleplay with AI in languages other than English and lorebooks don't work or you translate them yourself, check out my project Lorebook Gemini Translator (It works not only with Gemini).

docs.title: Main fields
docs.text:
• Base URL: A ready-to-use address for connecting to the API in your code or application.
  • Models: A list of key large language models available in the service. The 🌐 link usually leads to the full list.
  • Limits: API usage restrictions. RPM - requests per minute, RPH - per hour, RPD - per day.
  • Reliability: The author's subjective rating of the service's stability on a 5-star scale.

docs.title: Icon legend
docs.text:
• Navigation:

  • 🌐 - clickable link to the corresponding page (registration, getting a key, viewing models).

  • Testing status:

  • ✅ - tested by the author.
  • ❌ - service has not been tested yet.

  • ⏳ - in the process of testing.

  • Registration requirements:

  • ✉️ - email is required.
  • 🔑 - standard registration on the website.
  • 📱 - requires phone number verification.
  • 💳 - linking a bank card is required.
  • 📝❗ - registration has special conditions (e.g., only via a GitHub account).

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
• Freemium providers - providers that are not completely free, but provide credits/money to your account upon registration.
  • Free providers - providers that offer access to models absolutely for free.
  • Paid - services that require payment or operate on a credit-based system.
  • Dangerous / Not Recommended - providers with serious community concerns or trust issues.

docs.title: Dangerous / Not Recommended
docs.text:
Danger

These providers are listed here due to serious community concerns, repeated accusations, unethical behavior, or major trust issues. I do not recommend using them, and I intentionally do not provide direct links to their services.

docs.title: Free providers
docs.text:
NOTE

Providers in this list offer access to models absolutely for free, but may have certain restrictions (limits).

docs.title: NVIDIA NIM
docs.text:
Requirements Limits 🔗Models Reliability Testing ✉️ 🔑 📱 RPM - 40 🌐 • DeepSeek v4 flash/pro • kimi-k2 • glm-4.7/5.1 ⭐⭐⭐ ✅ 🔗 Registration 🔗 API key 🔗 Base URL 🌐 🌐 https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1

  • Models are unstable during peak hours (US daytime)

docs.title: OpenRouter
docs.text:
Requirements Limits 🔗Models Reliability Testing ✉️ 🔑 • RPM - 20 • RPD - 50 / 1000 *after payment 🌐 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ ✅ 🔗 Registration 🔗 API key 🔗 Base URL 🌐 🌐 https://openrouter.ai/api/v1

Features

  • Very large list of models.
  • Different companies very often publicly test their models, and most of the time they are free.
  • Not exactly a provider and not exactly a proxy; OpenRouter doesn't host models itself, but uses only official providers.

Disadvantages

  • To get an RPD higher than 50, you need to add $10 to your account, and you will get 1000 RPD.
  • Stability depends on the providers.

I apologize to NavyAI for the reputational loss this has caused. My mistake was that I didn't fully understand the situation and quickly took sides. It was completely my stupid mistake and I was wrong.

docs.title: Paid
docs.text:
NOTE

This section includes services that require payment or operate on a credit-based system. They may offer higher reliability, better performance, priority access, or fewer limitations compared to free providers.

WARNING

Some of these services have been personally tested or used during evaluation. This section reflects my own observations and impressions, which may include both positive and negative feedback depending on the service. It is not intended as a recommendation - always review pricing, limits, and data/privacy policies before use.
